claims.text: Partial replacement of heavier elements in an AlCoCrFeNi-like alloy by Ti or V reduces the alloy's bulk density.
The proposed as-cast lightweight AlCoCrFeNi-derived alloy has a predominantly single-phase microstructure.
An optimized post-cast annealing treatment can nucleate uniformly distributed, coherent nanoscale precipitates, such as Ti-rich precipitates, in the proposed alloy.
The heat-treatment-induced precipitates will occur within grains and along grain boundaries.
Coherent nanoprecipitates generate local stress fields that hinder dislocation motion.
Hindering dislocation motion through nanoprecipitation increases yield strength by precipitation hardening.
Coherent precipitate interfaces act as preferential nucleation sites for finely distributed, stable, adherent protective oxide or passivation films.
Precipitate-assisted passivation improves chloride corrosion resistance.
Precipitate-assisted protective oxide formation improves oxidation resistance at 800–950 °C.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the optimized heat-treated alloy will have significantly higher yield strength.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the optimized heat-treated alloy will exhibit improved corrosion resistance.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the optimized heat-treated alloy will exhibit improved high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The improved environmental resistance will be accompanied by a more uniform and adherent passivation layer.
Heat-treatment temperatures above approximately 1000 °C can cause precipitate coarsening in the proposed alloy.
Over-aging or excessive treatment duration makes the precipitate distribution non-uniform or otherwise detrimental.
Precipitate coarsening or over-aging eliminates the mechanical and environmental benefits of nanoscale precipitation.
A Ti80Nb10Mo5Sn5 medium-entropy alloy developed alpha precipitates at beta grain boundaries after room-temperature precipitation hardening and showed a 51% yield-strength increase.
Treated Ti80Nb10Mo5Sn5 samples exhibited pitting potentials above 1.8 V, no observed pitting holes, and an oxide layer containing TiO2, Nb2O5, MoO3, and SnO2.
Rapid annealing can promote nucleation, limit recrystallized-grain coarsening, and improve mechanical properties through grain-boundary strengthening.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that coarsening is an expected condition under which the hypothesis ceases to apply, whereas the falsification rule treats observation of uncontrolled coarsening as itself falsifying the nanoprecipitation mechanism. Coarsening would instead show that the intended mediator was not successfully produced and therefore would not decisively test that mechanism.
